newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends up on FDA proposal, export talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends up on FDA proposal, export talk.

text.p: CBOT soybean meal futures ended the session with sharp gains, after rallying on news that the U.S. government proposed banning ruminant tissue use in animal feed and on talk of export business to China, traders said.
Soyoil futures also ended sharply higher, mostly on commodity fund buying that was said to be short covering, floor traders said.

A U.S. Food and Drug Administration proposal to ban the use of meat and bone meal from ruminant animals in feed for ruminant animals like cattle and sheep, spurred ideas that demand for soymeal would grow and in turn, lifted futures, traders said.
There was also talk of a recent purchase of U.S. soymeal by China, but the deal could not be confirmed. China was said to have bought 50,000 tonnes U.S. soymeal for shipment during January.
Traders said spread activity in soyoil futures was heavy Thursday and it was that trade that initially triggered the rally in futures.
Soyoil futures ended 0.25 to 0.32 cent per lb higher, with January up 0.32 at 23.03 cents. Soymeal futures ended $2.30 to $4.00 per ton higher, with January up $2.30 at $228.60 a ton.
In soymeal trading, Rosenthal Collins bought 600 lots March, Griffin Trading bought 400 March, Paine Webber bought 500 lots January, ADM sold 100 lots January and 200 lots March, traders said.
In soyoil trade, Rosenthal bought 1,300 lots March and Paine Webber sold 800 lots March.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 25,000 contracts, above the 21,550 traded Tuesday.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 26,000 contracts, above the 16,927 contracts traded Tuesday.
